enrichment.markdown:
- **Rose (Roza) Goldfarb and family.** The accessible JewishGen page for the memorial book’s family section gives dates absent from the supplied passage: Rose died July 29, 1933; her husband, Shmuel Goldfarb, died January 20, 1934, and was a businessman born in Kobrin. It also names their seven children—Sarah Blumenfeld, Evelyn Levinson, Frances Citron, Marion Eskov, Esther Stone, Alger D. Goldfarb and Hazel Rogers—and records several of their later U.S. locations. The page’s family tree adds some descendants, including grandchildren and great-grandchildren, but is not an independent civil or archival record. [JewishGen, pp. 408–409](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/drohichyn/dro408.html)

- **Aaron and Hannah (Chana) Dragitchinsky; the wider family.** The same tree identifies Rose as one of Aaron and Chana’s children and places her among a larger sibling network, including John Mayer, Hinda, Feigel, Elka, Sarah and Tila. Its spelling varies—*Drogitchinsky*, *Dragitsinsky*—so the forms should be treated as transliteration variants, not separate families without further evidence. The book also describes Aaron’s role in Drohitchin community life, including support for the New House of Study; that provides local context, but does not establish any additional detail about Rose’s own life. [JewishGen family section](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/drohichyn/dro408.html); [JewishGen, p. 219](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/drohichyn/dro219.html)

- **Leo, Eva and Baron de Hirsh Mayer; Miami Beach.** The family section identifies Leo, Eva and Baron de Hirsh as children of John Mayer and Sarah Yaskulka, Rose’s relatives through the Dragitchinsky family. It describes Baron as an attorney, banker and philanthropist in Miami Beach, with roles at local Jewish and civic institutions. The page supplies no comparable biographical detail for Leo or Eva. These are family-book accounts, not independently verified records. [JewishGen, pp. 408–409](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/drohichyn/dro408.html)

- **Meir Faikav / Paykov.** The book’s English translation calls him Meir Paykov and identifies him as a family member killed by the Germans in Europe during the war. I found no corroborating record for the supplied spelling *Faikav* or the variant *Paykov* in the permitted search results, so his precise relationship, location and fate beyond the memorial-book statement remain unverified. [JewishGen, p. 409](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/drohichyn/dro408.html)

- **Search limits and place context.** Searches across the permitted-domain results for Rose/Roza Goldfarb, Shmuel/Samuel Goldfarb, Dragitchinsky/Drogitchinsky, and the linked Mayer and Paykov names surfaced the JewishGen memorial-book pages but no independently corroborating archival entries. Drohitchin (also rendered Drahichyn, Drogichin and Drohiczyn Poleski) and Kobrin are neighboring towns in today’s Belarusian regional geography; the Yizkor-book project notes that Drohitchin is about 33 miles east of Kobrin. [JewishGen town overview](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/ybip/YBIP_Drahichyn.html)
